inlines.text: Translate 2 units left and 2 units down. Centre

answer.worked:
Replace $x$ by $x+2$ and $y$ by $y+2$. This translates the graph 2 units left and 2 units down.

$$\begin{align*}(x+2)^2-(y+2)^2&=1\end{align*}$$

The centre is $(-2,-2)$ and the vertices are $(-3,-2)$ and $(-1,-2)$. Translate the original asymptotes in the same way:

$$\begin{align*}y+2&=x+2\\y&=x\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y+2&=-(x+2)\\y&=-x-4\end{align*}$$

Sketch the two branches opening left and right through the translated vertices, approaching these asymptotes.
